body:
Deployment_Properties declares Actual_Connection_Binding as a list of
reference to (processor, virtual processor, bus, virtual bus, device,
memory, system, abstract). A cross-processor connection bound to a memory
was nonetheless warned "…which is a memory — not a bus or virtual bus".

Now the binding target is resolved by identity from the component that
declared it (a value on the connection from the connection's context, a
value on the owner from the owner's), replacing a model-wide name search
(unambiguous_non_bus_category, deleted). By target category: bus or virtual
bus -> no diagnostic (as before); memory -> an Info line naming the memory
as the transport; any other category -> the warning, now worded "not a bus,
virtual bus or memory".

Oracle: crates/spar-cli/tests/wrpc_binding_memory.rs (5 tests: memory
binding gives one INFO and no warning; inline and applies-to forms agree;
an unbound crossing still warns; a binding to a process still warns; a
memory on a same-processor connection is silent) plus 4 unit tests. On
origin/main the memory test fails with the "not a bus" warning; with this
change 5/5. Disabling the memory arm by hand turns it red again (4/1).

Corpus (2091 .aadl files, 1550 runs, diff -ra): 1 run differs, 3 lines in
aadlib multicore/avionicsbusmanagers.aadl whose wording changes to include
"or memory" (bound to a system; severity unchanged). No corpus model binds
a connection to a memory, so only the tests exercise the new path.

cargo-mutants --in-diff generated only 2 mutants (1 caught, 1 unviable);
match arms are not mutated, hence the hand mutation above.

Not changed: processor, virtual processor, device, system and abstract are
also legal targets and still warn; whether they are transports is a
separate decision. An Actual_Connection_Binding to a name that resolves
nowhere is reported by no analysis, on this branch or on v0.47.1; tracked
separately.

Refs #515, REQ-WRPC-BINDING-MEMORY-001 (v0.48.0)
